source_snapshot.title: Quantitative trace-reconstruction bounds with a uniform decoder
source_snapshot.status: source statements inspected; proof not independently verified; no formal replay

claims.statement: For fixed q in (0,1), let d_n=min_{x!=y in {0,1}^n} TV(D_q(x),D_q(y)). The family-122 source asserts n^A d_n -> 0 for every fixed A>0. For every polynomial m(n)<=n^r, an equal-prior minimizing pair has optimal identification success at most 1/2+o(1) from m(n) independent complete deletion traces.
assumptions: q is fixed and known in (0,1)
each position is independently deleted with probability q
each observation is the complete surviving word and its length, with order preserved and no original position labels
traces are independent samples from the same deterministic input string
the codebook contains the minimizing pair; automatic for the unrestricted binary-string tag universe
claims.status: conditional transfer; source theorem source-reported; product-TV and binary-testing consequence internally derived
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, sections Result and status and Exact application contract
claims.novelty_boundary: The deletion lower bound is a source claim, not a new theorem here. The contribution is an interface-level transfer to an idealized binary molecular tag and an explicit hard-pair/codebook condition. No biological or priority claim.

costs.read_samples: m per tag; lower bound is independent of decoder compute
costs.exposed_sequence_symbols: at most m*n bases per tag
costs.multiple_tags: K independently decoded tags require K*m reads at the same per-tag budget before pool dropout and amplification costs

claims.falsifier: An error in the source hard-pair theorem or in the iid product-TV/two-point-testing calculation; for the application, a codebook excluding the hard pair or a physical channel supplying additional position information voids the transfer premises.
claims.next_gate: Materialize source hard pairs at finite n, replay the ideal deletion channel, then test an equally long codebook control under a calibrated physical channel while auditing all sequence constraints.

claims.statement: The subclass of length-n binary words whose successive ones are separated by at least L=Theta(log^8 n) zeros has log2 cardinality O(n log log n/log^8 n)=o(n), so this sufficient mildly-separated reconstruction class has vanishing asymptotic rate.
assumptions: at least L zeros between every pair of successive ones
claims.status: internally derived counting bound; not a bound on all decodable codebooks
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section What code design can change
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary cardinality consequence of the separated-string premise; not claimed as new. It only quantifies rate loss in this sufficient subclass.

costs.encoding_rate: o(1) information bits per base in this subclass
costs.reconstruction_samples: Aamand-Liu-Narayanan theorem gives O(n log n) traces under its deletion-rate and gap hypotheses

claims.falsifier: A counting error in the maximum-weight bound sum_{t<=r} binom(n,t) with r=1+(n-1)/(L+1).
claims.next_gate: Check any proposed molecular sequence filter against actual rate and the exact ALN assumptions; do not generalize to arbitrary codebooks.

claims.statement: High-rate coded recovery is compatible with the arbitrary-input deletion lower bound: binary code families of rate 1-epsilon have a primary-source recovery guarantee using a trace count depending on fixed q and epsilon but not on n.
assumptions: a designed binary codebook is used
the code's decoder and construction premises apply
claims.status: primary-literature result; not independently verified here
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section What code design can change
claims.novelty_boundary: Established prior art; cited to prevent overgeneralizing the source lower bound. Compatibility with biochemical filters and full DNA-storage channels is not provided by the cited theorem.

costs.sample_count: exp(O_q(log^(1/3)(1/epsilon))) for fixed q, epsilon; independent of n
costs.sequence_constraints: not covered by the abstract coded-trace theorem

claims.falsifier: A mismatch between the stated primary theorem and its actual code/decoder channel assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Determine whether a specific DNA sequence-constrained code construction retains the theorem's rate and sample guarantee under the measured physical channel.

claims.statement: Conditional on the family-332 finite-range global extension premise, every Lipschitz map from an arbitrary subset S of any metric source X with finite Markov type-2 constant into ambient real L1(Omega,mu), for any positive measure space, extends to X with Lip(F) <= C_MN*12*sqrt(21)*M2(X)*Lip(f). The arbitrary-range and nonseparable-source conclusion follows from product weak-star compactness in L1** and the norm-one L-embedded projection.
assumptions: Real-valued ambient L1; the cut proof does not establish the complex-valued case
The family-332 real-ell_1 metric Markov cotype theorem and finite exact cut recovery are accepted as conditional premises
Every finite boundary restriction has a global L1-valued extension with a uniform constant
C_MN is the unspecified universal constant from Mendel-Naor Corollary 1.13
L1(mu) is L-embedded for the given positive measure space
claims.status: internally proved conditional theorem; compactness mechanism is standard; source cotype theorem is not externally proof-validated
claims.novelty_boundary: Naor 2609.07564v2 explicitly states arbitrary-subset ell_2-to-Lebesgue-L1 extension and reports forthcoming Mendel-Naor work proving L1 metric Markov cotype 2. Thus standard Lebesgue-L1 consequences are preempted at statement level. The broader arbitrary-positive-measure real-L1 transfer is not explicit in the inspected Naor v2; priority remains UNKNOWN.

costs.algorithm: Nonconstructive bidual compactness; no runtime, finite representation, or numerical stability guarantee

claims.falsifier: A flaw in the family-332 cotype result, finite exact cut recovery, or arbitrary-measure L-embeddedness would invalidate this conditional transfer.
claims.next_gate: Inspect the forthcoming MN26 proof when available; compare exact measure-space scope/constants; obtain independent proof review of family 332.

overall_conclusion: Model-level cross-field transfer only. No experiment, proof validation, novelty search beyond cited primary prior art, or clinical inference was performed. Cycle 3 metric extension result is a standard bidual compactness consequence of the conditional finite-range L1 premise; Naor 2609.07564v2 preempts the standard Lebesgue-L1 extension statement, while arbitrary-measure scope priority remains UNKNOWN.
